items.stem: Which Step Functions state type is used to choose between branches based on input?

options.rationale: Correct: a Choice state branches execution based on input conditions.
A Task state does work; it does not branch.
A Pass state forwards input without branching.
A Succeed state ends execution successfully.

items.stem: Which TWO are true when choosing between Standard and Express workflows? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Standard suits long-running, auditable workflows with full execution history
options.rationale: Correct: Standard retains full history and supports long durations.

options.text: Express suits very high-volume, short-duration workloads
options.rationale: Correct: Express is optimized for high event rates and short runs.

options.text: Express keeps unlimited full execution history for a year by default
options.rationale: Express has limited history retention, unlike Standard.

options.text: Standard is always cheaper than Express at any volume
options.rationale: Cost depends on volume and duration; neither is always cheaper.

items.explanation: Correct: Standard suits long-running, auditable workflows with full execution history, Express suits very high-volume, short-duration workloads.

items.stem: How should a task that may fail transiently be made more resilient in a state machine?

options.text: Add a Retry policy with backoff, and a Catch for a fallback
options.rationale: Correct: Retry with backoff handles transient failures; Catch routes to a fallback.

options.text: Remove all error handling so it fails fast every time
options.rationale: Removing handling makes transient failures fatal.
Transient errors do occur and must be handled.
Deleting the task removes the work, not the error risk.

items.explanation: Correct: Add a Retry policy with backoff, and a Catch for a fallback.
